summary: Preserve that a derived constructor may return an object without ever initializing this via super(), and that object becomes the construction result.

target.notes: Use the JavaScript construction path; a normal C# derived constructor cannot skip base construction and return an unrelated object.

semantics.derived_instance_brand: not necessarily present unless private elements are stamped by the class initialization path

caveats: C# requires a base constructor chain for normal object creation and constructors cannot return replacement objects.

tests.name: derived object return without super
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { constructor(){ return {x:1}; } } console.log(new D().x);

tests.name: edge: returned object is not D prototype instance
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { constructor(){ return {}; } } console.log(new D() instanceof D);
